stem: A 6-year-old girl has breast development and vaginal bleeding. Serum LH and FSH are low, estradiol and inhibin are markedly high, and pelvic imaging shows a solid ovarian mass.
oneliner: 6F + breast development + vaginal bleeding + low LH/FSH + very high estradiol and inhibin + solid ovarian mass → which cell type?
ask: From which cell type did this tumor most likely arise?

whyNot.A: Make **androgens** and cause virilization, not **breast development with high estradiol**
whyNot.B: Give **dysgerminoma, teratoma or yolk sac** tumors; they do not make **estrogen and inhibin**
whyNot.C: Gives **serous or mucinous** tumors, usually in older women, that do not make **estrogen**
whyNot.E: Give an **ovarian fibroma**, which makes **no estrogen or inhibin**

why: Low gonadotropins with high estrogen from an ovarian mass means **gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty** from a **granulosa cell tumor**, a **sex cord-stromal tumor**. Granulosa cells contain **aromatase**, which makes estrogen, and also secrete **inhibin**, a tumor marker.

idea.rule: Granulosa cell tumor = sex cord-stromal tumor that makes estrogen (aromatase) and inhibin.
also: Causes precocious puberty in girls and postmenopausal bleeding in older women
Raised estrogen predisposes to endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma
Call-Exner bodies are typical of the adult type
Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors instead make androgens (virilization)
